questions.prompt: A camera reads 4.0 m with variance 0.25 and a lidar reads 3.6 m with variance 0.04. What is the inverse-variance fused depth (4 decimals)?
What is the variance of that fused estimate (4 decimals)?
Two sensors disagree with d^2 = 13.8 against the 3.84 threshold. What is the correct reading of this?
options: Both sensors are certainly fine, since the disagreement is within normal noise.
The lidar is the faulty sensor, since it disagrees more with the camera.
The fused variance should be halved, because two sensors agree on average.
At least one sensor is biased, blinded or has understated variance; the test cannot say which.
questions.explanation: d^2 > 3.84 is rare (5%) for consistent noise; the test flags inconsistency, not the culprit.

questions.prompt: A model says it is 95% confident on average but is right 80% of the time. It is
Five predictions: confidences 0.9, 0.9, 0.8, 0.6, 0.6 and outcomes 1, 1, 0, 1, 0. Compute ECE with two bins split at 0.75 (2 decimals).
questions.explanation: High bin gap 0.2 x 3/5 = 0.12; low bin gap 0.1 x 2/5 = 0.04; total 0.16.

questions.prompt: An evaluation reports mean accuracy over clean, occlusion, noise and fog of 0.77. Why is this a weak summary for a safety-relevant robot?
options: Fog is never relevant to the safety of a robot in operation.
The mean can hide a single condition in which the system fails badly.
The mean is not defined for a set of exactly four numbers.
Accuracy values cannot be averaged across different conditions.
questions.explanation: Report the worst case and per-condition numbers.

questions.prompt: Design an evaluation suite for a perception module that fuses a camera and a lidar. Name the shifts and severities, the metrics, the baseline, a boundary case and a rejection rule.
rubric: Names concrete shifts with severities (occlusion, noise, fog, sensor dropout).
Reports per-condition and worst-case metrics against a clean baseline and a single-sensor baseline.
Includes the boundary case of all sensors failing and a rejection rule.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
